func (t *PrepareReply) Marshal(wire io.Writer) {
	var b [18]byte
	var bs []byte
	bs = b[:17]
	tmp32 := t.AcceptorId
	bs[0] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[1] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[2] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[3] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	tmp32 = t.Replica
	bs[4] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[5] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[6] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[7] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	tmp32 = t.Instance
	bs[8] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[9] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[10] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[11] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	tmp32 = t.Ballot
	bs[12] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[13] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[14] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[15] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	bs[16] = byte(t.Status)
	wire.Write(bs)
	bs = b[:]
	alen1 := int64(len(t.Command))
	if wlen := binary.PutVarint(bs, alen1); wlen >= 0 {
		wire.Write(b[0:wlen])
	}
	for i := int64(0); i < alen1; i++ {
		t.Command[i].Marshal(wire)
	}
	bs = b[:4]
	tmp32 = t.Seq
	bs[0] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[1] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[2] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[3] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	wire.Write(bs)
	bs = b[:]
	alen2 := int64(len(t.Deps))
	if wlen := binary.PutVarint(bs, alen2); wlen >= 0 {
		wire.Write(b[0:wlen])
	}
	for i := int64(0); i < alen2; i++ {
		bs = b[:4]
		tmp32 = t.Deps[i]
		bs[0] = byte(tmp32)
		bs[1] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
		bs[2] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
		bs[3] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
		wire.Write(bs)
	}
}

		-1,
		batchWait,

	}

	r.Beacon = beacon

	for i := 0; i < r.N; i++ {

	r.preAcceptRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(PreAccept), r.preAcceptChan)

	r.commitRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(Commit), r.commitChan)
	r.tryPreAcceptRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(TryPreAccept), r.tryPreAcceptChan)

	go r.run()

	return r

formation.explanation: A proposal is batched into its receiving replica row and starts phase 1 with owner-ID ballot. Conflict indices establish Seq/Deps. Thrifty PreAccept reaches selected alive peers, whose reports are qualified by lastTriedBallot and phase status. The owner merges attributes and either fast commits under threshold/equality/initial-ballot conditions (with a small-cluster exception) or broadcasts Accept and commits after a majority count. Full Commit carries commands and attributes; receivers reject stale ballots and already established decisions. Default Dreply=true delays client response until dependency/SCC execution. Sender and receiver codecs, not just handler structs, are part of this relationship.

context.explanation: Authority is per row/instance. inst.bal guards incoming work; leader bookkeeping lastTriedBallot guards phase replies. Executor-driven recovery replaces local attempt bookkeeping while retaining proposals and stored value; generated ballots depend on ID/N and optionally maxRecvBallot under master-granted IsLeader. Prepare raises the promise and reports prior vbal/status/attributes. A slow quorum including the self report selects support using VBallot, then preserves a reported committed state, accepts retained support, or restarts phase 1. Prior committed instances with commands bypass recovery. No global revocation mechanism was found; stale work is handled by these local promise/status/phase checks, whose actual strength remains investigable.

connection.explanation: Recovery authority does not independently determine a new value: its consumer uses reported support provenance/status and attributes to decide which formation path is eligible. bal may rise while vbal and prior attributes remain in handlePrepare, separating promise from support. The local recovery entry instead updates both ballots before self reporting; remote replies cross a codec that omits VBallot. These discrepancies are unresolved premises of support preservation, not assumed agreement failures. Old phase replies face attempt/phase guards; established commit messages have status/ballot guards. Pending client proposals are retained across recovery and sometimes requeued after NOOP; consumption still requires complete committed dependencies.

func (t *PrepareReply) Marshal(wire io.Writer) {
	var b [18]byte
	var bs []byte
	bs = b[:17]
	tmp32 := t.AcceptorId
	bs[0] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[1] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[2] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[3] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	tmp32 = t.Replica
	bs[4] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[5] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[6] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[7] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	tmp32 = t.Instance
	bs[8] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[9] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[10] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[11] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	tmp32 = t.Ballot
	bs[12] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[13] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[14] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[15] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	bs[16] = byte(t.Status)
	wire.Write(bs)
	bs = b[:]
	alen1 := int64(len(t.Command))
	if wlen := binary.PutVarint(bs, alen1); wlen >= 0 {
		wire.Write(b[0:wlen])
	}
	for i := int64(0); i < alen1; i++ {
		t.Command[i].Marshal(wire)
	}
	bs = b[:4]
	tmp32 = t.Seq
	bs[0] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[1] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[2] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[3] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	wire.Write(bs)
	bs = b[:]
	alen2 := int64(len(t.Deps))
	if wlen := binary.PutVarint(bs, alen2); wlen >= 0 {
		wire.Write(b[0:wlen])
	}
	for i := int64(0); i < alen2; i++ {
		bs = b[:4]
		tmp32 = t.Deps[i]
		bs[0] = byte(tmp32)
		bs[1] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
		bs[2] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
		bs[3] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
		wire.Write(bs)
	}
}

		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0,
		make([][]*Instance, len(peerAddrList)),
		make([]int32, len(peerAddrList)),
		make([]int32, len(peerAddrList)),
		make([]int32, len(peerAddrList)),
		nil,
		make([]map[state.Key]*InstPair, len(peerAddrList)),
		make(map[state.Key]int32),
		0,
		0,
		-1,
		new(sync.Mutex),
		make(chan *instanceId, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		false,
		-1,
		batchWait,
		transconf,
	}

	r.Beacon = beacon
	r.Durable = durable

	for i := 0; i < r.N; i++ {
		r.InstanceSpace[i] = make([]*Instance, MAX_INSTANCE) // FIXME
		r.crtInstance[i] = -1
		r.ExecedUpTo[i] = -1
		r.CommittedUpTo[i] = -1
		r.conflicts[i] = make(map[state.Key]*InstPair, HT_INIT_SIZE)
	}

	r.exec = &Exec{r}

	cpMarker = make([]state.Command, 0)

	//register RPCs
	r.prepareRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(Prepare), r.prepareChan)

Prepare raises the promise and reports prior vbal/status/attributes. A slow quorum including the self report selects support using VBallot, then preserves a reported committed state, accepts retained support, or restarts phase 1. Prior committed instances with commands bypass recovery. No global revocation mechanism was found; stale work is handled by these local promise/status/phase checks, whose actual strength remains investigable.

connection.explanation: Recovery authority does not independently determine a new value: its consumer uses reported support provenance/status and attributes to decide which formation path is eligible. bal may rise while vbal and prior attributes remain in handlePrepare, separating promise from support. The local recovery entry instead updates both ballots before self reporting; remote replies cross a codec that omits VBallot. The remote codec discrepancy has a reviewed local witness; local self-provenance and wider agreement consequences remain unresolved. Old phase replies face attempt/phase guards; established commit messages have status/ballot guards. Pending client proposals are retained across recovery and sometimes requeued after NOOP; consumption still requires complete committed dependencies.
